name: init_record_state_handler
description: Links the record at the argument pointer into a list head held in a global slot, sets its state flag and a timer value chosen from a counter, then installs this routine as its per-frame handler before restoring the previous list head.

name: init_record_from_argument
description: Links the record passed in the address register into a list head held in a global slot, applies the same counter-selected timer values as its sibling initialiser, then installs itself as the record's handler and restores the previous list head. It returns the saved data registers unchanged.

name: step_record_timers_by_mode
description: Clears a per-record counter, then adjusts two timer fields depending on a global mode value: halving one with a floor, decrementing the other, or in the default case setting bit flags and resetting both timers and the handler. It calls the unnamed routine in every branch.

name: reset_counters_then_step_timers
description: Writes two fixed constants into global words and clears another global word, then runs the same mode-dependent timer step as the neighbouring routine on the current record. It is a setup-then-update routine for the same record layout.

name: halve_value_with_minimum
description: Adds five to a 16-bit field of the record, halves the sum, raises the result to a minimum read from a global word, and stores it back. It is a simple clamped halving with no calls.

name: dispatch_bit_mask_to_handler
description: Calls the unnamed routine, then tests the low flag bits of a state word in order and, for the first bit found set, stores a sub-state value and the next handler address. When no bit is set it sets an extra flag bit and selects a fallback handler.

name: dispatch_handler_by_address_match
description: Compares the handler pointer of an object against a long chain of candidate handler addresses, and for each match adds fixed increments of 10, 50, 100 or 200 to a counter, updates sprite-like list fields, or sets flag bits. It ends by jumping through an unrecovered jump table, and the listing is cut off so only its opening part is evident.

name: prepare_and_start_blit
description: Calls two unnamed routines, loads a stored destination pointer, and waits for the blitter to become idle before writing its data, modulo and mask registers and then its size register, which starts the blit. A second busy wait follows to let it finish.

name: start_blit_from_stored_pointer
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, loads the destination pointer from a stored slot, clears the blitter data and modulo registers, sets the mask and control registers and writes the blit size to start it. It waits again for completion.

name: init_record_if_unset_flag
description: Returns at once when a global flag is set; otherwise it increments a counter, looks up an entry by the value from a call, and if the record's status byte is zero or negative it copies fixed initial constants into the record, installs a handler and sets a flag.

name: start_blit_with_fixed_size
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, loads a source pointer from a stored block, clears the data registers, sets a fixed modulo and a fixed blit size, and waits again until the blit finishes. The size values are constants written straight into the custom chip registers.

name: or_combine_bitplane_rows
description: Over a block of six rows and twenty columns, ORs the bytes from four bitplane source rows and writes the combined byte to four destination rows spaced one bitplane row apart. It has no calls and only reads and writes memory.

name: decode_keyboard_code_toggles
description: Reads a raw keyboard byte from a global that the keyboard serial register supplies, ignores it unless its valid bit is set, and toggles one of four flag bits for each matching code. Two other codes adjust a step counter, and the function then refreshes a status byte from the flags.

name: decode_keyboard_code_from_register
description: Performs the same keyboard code decoding as its sibling routine, but takes the key byte from the data register and returns the decoded value. It toggles the same flag bits and step counter.

name: reset_status_and_clear_counters
description: Calls one unnamed routine, clears a global status byte and clears two 16-bit counters. The bit tests that follow read the byte just cleared, so the conditional table updates are never taken.

name: clear_flags_and_select_status
description: Clears the flag word, calls three unnamed routines, then selects a status code from the flag bits and increments a frame counter. The status selection writes one of two mode letters into a global byte.

name: merge_status_byte_into_flags
description: Copies a non-zero status byte into the top flag bits, toggles an extra flag group, then selects the status code from those flags and increments a frame counter. It shares the status selection code of its sibling routine.

name: select_status_code_from_flags
description: Selects one of two mode letters into a global status byte from a set of flag bits and a readiness word, then increments a frame counter. It makes one unnamed routine call and no other changes to memory.

name: claim_free_node_and_place
description: Takes the head node from a free list and returns if the list is empty; otherwise it copies two position words from the source record into the node, offsets one of them, sets its handler and counters, and records it in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value. It is a pool allocator for a fixed set of nodes.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: claim_node_and_track_slot
description: Takes the head node from a free list and returns if it is empty, otherwise it copies two position words from the source record, sets a timer and handler, and places the node in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value, using a fixed code. It is a pool claim with a different offset and timer from its neighbours.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: spawn_three_nodes_when_clear
description: When a computed position difference exceeds two and the free list has a node, it claims up to three pool nodes in turn, each with its own horizontal offset, a shared step value and a timer. Each claimed node gets the same handler and a counter increment on the source record.

name: spawn_four_nodes_when_clear
description: When a computed position difference exceeds three and the free list has a node, it claims up to four pool nodes in turn, each with its own horizontal offset and timer. Each node is placed in the same way as its sibling spawner.

name: spawn_three_nodes_alternate_offsets
description: Claims up to three pool nodes in turn when a position difference exceeds two, giving each a different horizontal offset and a step value. It sets the same handler and counters as its sibling spawners.

name: spawn_node_quartered_threshold
description: When a quartered position value is not below the source record's field and a free node exists, it claims one node, sets its vertical word from a global that it toggles each time, and sets its timer. The node is then recorded in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: spawn_node_compared_to_input
description: When the input position is not below the source field and a free node exists, it claims one node, sets its vertical word from a global that it toggles, and assigns a timer and step. It then records the node in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: spawn_node_with_random_velocity
description: Claims one pool node when the input position is not below a source field, derives a sideways velocity of minus one, zero or plus one from a modulo of a running global value, and sets the vertical word from a toggled global. The node is recorded in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: spawn_node_with_offset_toggle
description: When the input position is not below the source field and a free node exists, it claims one node, sets its vertical word from a toggled global, and applies a different vertical step and timer from its neighbours. The node is then recorded in a tracking slot that is free or holds the lower value.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use. It has one instruction and does no work.

name: record_index_in_tracking_slot
description: Stores an index and a value read from a lookup table into one of two tracking slots, filling an empty slot first and otherwise replacing the slot holding the lower value. It is called by many routines to keep the two best entries.

name: init_twenty_six_pool_nodes
description: Loops twenty-six times over a pointer table, claiming a pool node for each entry, clearing its state and two words, setting two bytes from a returned value plus four and a fixed timer, and installing the record handler. Each claimed node is stored in the table.

name: init_twenty_six_pool_nodes
description: Performs the same twenty-six-entry node initialisation as its sibling routine, claiming pool nodes into the pointer table and setting their state, timer and handler fields. It has no other effects.

name: shift_record_positions_in_passes
description: Adjusts the two position words of a table of records in several passes with different counts, subtracting one global value, adding a fixed constant and adding another global value to each. The passes differ in their count and in which global values they use.

name: randomise_node_list_fields
description: Walks a linked list of nodes until a null link, clearing a state byte and two words in each and setting a byte from a running global value, reduced to a value from three to nine. The per-node value is derived from a pseudo-random sequence.

name: clear_node_states_until_null
description: Walks a table of up to twenty-six node pointers, stopping at the first empty entry, and clears a state byte in each node it reaches. It makes no calls and writes nothing else.

name: reset_idle_nodes_and_links
description: Walks a table of up to twenty-six node pointers and, for each node whose state byte is not three, clears its state and fields, sets a fixed timer and links it to entries from a secondary table while a counter stays non-negative. It finishes by clearing a global word.

name: reset_finished_nodes_and_globals
description: Walks a table of up to twenty-six node pointers, stopping at an empty entry, and resets each node in state three with a fixed timer, clear fields and a handler. It then clears four global words.

name: build_free_list_from_table
description: Clears the free list head and pushes each of twenty-six table nodes onto it, clearing their state, flag and field words and storing a returned byte into each one. This prepares a pool of nodes for later claiming.

name: clear_table_nodes_state_flags
description: Loops over a table of node pointers for a count held in a global, clearing each node's state and flag bytes and setting two words to minus one. It makes no calls.

name: clear_pointer_table_nodes
description: Makes three unnamed calls, then walks a table of node pointers whose length comes from a stored word, clearing each node's state byte and setting two words to minus one.

name: fill_node_table_with_bytes
description: Fills twenty-six table entries with nodes obtained from a source call, clearing each node's state and fields, and stores two returned byte values into each node.

name: fill_node_table_from_count
description: Fills a table of node pointers with nodes from a source call, with the count held in a global, and clears each node's state and words. Each entry is written before the next is taken.

name: fill_node_table_by_sum
description: Fills a code-pointer table whose length is the sum of two stored words, taking a node from a source call for each entry, storing it and clearing its state and words. The table is written as it is filled.

name: fill_node_table_by_sum
description: Performs the same node table fill as its sibling routine, taking nodes from a source call for each entry of a length given by two stored words. It clears each node's state and words.

name: mark_nodes_for_cleanup
description: Marks nodes for cleanup by setting their state byte to a special value in three passes: nodes with a positive state, nodes in state fourteen and nodes in state fifteen, plus everything on the active list tail. It then sets a timer word to two thousand and clears another word.

name: mark_nodes_for_cleanup
description: Performs the same cleanup marking as its sibling routine, setting node state bytes to a special value in the three passes and on the active list. It sets the timer word to two thousand and clears another word, with no return value.

name: build_pattern_table_from_bits
description: Clears five global words, then fills a small pattern table with shifted bit patterns, choosing one of two value sets for each of four bit positions in a global byte. Each entry is ORed into the existing table bytes.

name: run_with_saved_pointer
description: When a flag word is non-zero it swaps the current pointer for a saved one, runs an unnamed routine, then restores the pointer. It always runs a second unnamed routine afterwards.

name: set_pair_words_by_flags
description: Calls five unnamed routines, then for each of six flag bits set in a byte of the current object it writes a fixed constant into a pair of words in a structure reached through a pointer field.

name: clear_thirty_six_global_longs
description: Calls three unnamed routines, then clears thirty-six consecutive longwords starting at a global address. It is a simple block clear.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_to_buffer
description: When the object's state word is zero it clears a flag word, sets a derived position value from a quarter of another word, and copies a sixteen-longword table entry into the buffer the object points to. The table is selected by an index read from the object.

name: advance_position_and_copy_frame
description: Either runs an unnamed routine twice with a swapped pointer, or moves a position word by a velocity step within limits, writes it into a structure, and copies a sixteen-longword frame when the state flag changes. It exits early if the state is already set.

name: advance_position_and_copy_frame
description: Performs the same position step and frame copy as its sibling routine, with a 64-bit return value. It moves a position word by a velocity step within limits and copies a sixteen-longword frame on state change.

name: move_position_and_copy_frame
description: Moves a position word by a velocity step within limits, writes it into a structure, and copies a sixteen-longword frame into the buffer when the state flag changes. It does not have the pointer-swap branch of its siblings.

name: store_position_and_copy_frame
description: Stores a 16-bit position into the object, writes its halved value and low bit into a structure, and copies a sixteen-longword frame to the buffer when the state is not already set. It exits early otherwise.

name: rearrange_word_table_into_planes
description: Installs its handler and, on first call, rearranges a seventeen-row word table into three interleaved destination tables. It then copies ten words from the source into the destination rows and increments a counter byte.

name: rearrange_word_table_into_planes
description: Installs its handler and, on first call, rearranges a seventeen-row word table into three interleaved destination tables. It then copies ten words from the source into the destination rows and increments a counter byte.

name: rearrange_word_table_into_planes
description: Performs the same word-table rearrangement and ten-word copy as its sibling routine, installing its handler and bumping a counter byte. It differs only in its callers.

name: rescale_list_entries_by_offset
description: When a flag word is set, it walks a list of word pairs until a terminator, swapping two marker values and rescaling the high byte of other entries against an offset word while setting their low bit. Entries that match neither case are left unchanged.

name: render_score_digits_to_bitplanes
description: Converts a value below one hundred thousand into decimal digits and writes each digit's eight-row glyph into six bitplane rows; larger values are capped at five hundred thousand and fill the cells with a solid pattern. It then copies a six-byte pattern from a table to a fixed display location.

name: advance_counters_and_shift_entries
description: Advances counters over a table of eight-byte entries, moving entries down one slot when a flag and threshold hold, and toggles state bits; it touches the CIA and custom chip registers. The listing is cut off, so only this overall pattern is evident from the code.

name: update_pattern_animation_timers
description: Per-frame update that counts down an animation timer and, on expiry, XORs a set of pattern words in a shared buffer and steps a second countdown, writing fixed pattern constants when that ends. It also updates position words from a table and calls a follow-up routine when a countdown reaches zero.

name: update_pattern_animation_timers
description: Performs the same animation timer and pattern update as its sibling routine, without the leading guard that tests a global value. It otherwise matches its sibling's countdowns, XOR masks and follow-up call.

name: clear_thirty_six_global_longs
description: Calls eight unnamed routines, then clears thirty-six consecutive longwords starting at a global address. It is a simple block clear after setup calls.

name: clear_thirty_six_global_longs
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then clears thirty-six consecutive longwords starting at a global address. It is a simple block clear after setup calls.

name: call_routine_count_times
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then reads a count from a field of the current record and calls a second unnamed routine that many minus one times, provided the count is positive and not one. It is a counted repeat of an unnamed call.

name: copy_interleaved_word_pairs
description: Copies words from a source table in steps of eighty bytes into a destination, writing each source word and the word twenty places later as an adjacent pair, for a count held in a data register.

name: clear_longs_for_count
description: Clears consecutive longwords starting at a destination address for a count held in a data register. It is a simple block clear.

name: draw_four_entries_when_active
description: When the object's flag word is clear, it calls an unnamed routine, then for each of four entries with a non-zero word calls another unnamed routine with that entry's table pointer and a destination that advances by forty bytes.

name: set_pair_words_by_flags
description: After one unnamed call, for each of six flag bits set in the object's flag byte it writes a fixed constant into a pair of words in a structure reached through a pointer field. It mirrors the flag-to-word logic of its sibling routine.

name: set_entry_state_and_countdown
description: Sets the state, two position words and a timer on a record reached through a global pointer and bumps a global counter by two. When a countdown reaches zero it reloads it with a value one less than before, never below five, and calls an unnamed routine.

name: claim_first_idle_entry_randomised
description: Finds the first record in a table of twenty-six whose state byte is zero and sets its vertical word to a pseudo-random value from thirty to one hundred twenty-nine. It also picks one of two fixed sideways values from a pseudo-random bit, sets a timer of three hundred and installs a handler.

name: render_eight_digit_field
description: Either calls an unnamed routine or fills two longwords with a fixed pattern, depending on a computed limit of one hundred million. It then copies eight characters from a text string into six bitplane rows through a glyph table, clears several globals and calls an unnamed routine.

name: run_routine_pairs_swapped
description: Saves the current record pointer, points it at a global block to run two unnamed routines, then points it at another routine to run two more, and finally restores the saved pointer. It is a context switch around a set of calls.

name: run_routine_pairs_swapped
description: Performs the same save, pointer swap, two-routine call pairs and restore as its sibling routine. It differs only in its callers.

name: run_routine_pairs_swapped
description: Performs the same save, pointer swap, two-routine call pairs and restore as its sibling routines. It has no other effects.

name: render_eight_glyph_columns
description: Calls an unnamed routine first, then if a global flag is set it swaps the current pointer for each of two saved pointers and runs a routine on each. Otherwise it copies eight glyph bytes, each looked up from a record byte, into six bitplane rows of a display buffer.

name: render_eight_glyph_columns
description: Performs the same flag-driven pointer swap or eight-byte glyph copy as its sibling routine. It writes six bitplane rows from record bytes through a glyph table.

name: render_eight_glyph_columns
description: Performs the same eight-glyph copy into six bitplane rows as its sibling routines, taking the flag-driven pointer swap as its alternative branch. It returns the value of the last call made.

name: copy_eight_glyph_columns
description: Copies eight glyph bytes, each looked up from a record byte, into six bitplane rows of a display buffer, with no pointer swap. It returns the value it was given.

name: copy_eight_glyph_columns
description: Performs the same eight-glyph copy into six bitplane rows as its sibling routine, looking each glyph up from a record byte. It has no other branches.

name: add_table_digits_to_score
description: Adds per-digit increments from a table, selected by a state word, to a ten-digit decimal counter held as bytes in a record, rippling carries upward. When the top digit overflows it calls an unnamed routine; the listing is cut off, so the tail of the routine is not evident.

name: carry_step_across_eight_bytes
description: Adds a step byte to a run of consecutive bytes ending at the address register, and when a byte reaches a threshold it subtracts the threshold and carries the step into the next byte, for up to eight bytes.

name: wait_until_flag_cleared
description: Stores a value from a data register into a global word and spins until that word is cleared to zero by another part of the program. It makes no calls.

name: run_frame_update_loop
description: Waits for a frame flag, then for each active node in a linked list advances its position and velocity words, reflecting them at fixed bounds, and waits for the blitter to go idle before writing the node's values into blitter registers. The listing is cut off, so the tail of the loop is not evident.

name: run_frame_update_loop
description: Performs the same frame-synchronised update of linked-list node positions, bounds reflection and blitter register writes as its sibling routine. Only its opening assignments differ.

name: run_frame_update_loop
description: Performs the same frame-synchronised update of linked-list node positions, bounds reflection and blitter register writes as its sibling routines. Only its opening assignments differ.

name: run_frame_update_loop
description: Performs the same frame-synchronised node update and blitter writes as its siblings, and also touches the CIA chip registers. The listing is cut off, so the full sequence is not evident.

name: randomise_node_motion_values
description: Writes pseudo-random initial motion values into a node: one horizontal value from a larger range, a cleared longword and two further signed values from smaller ranges. The values come from the shared random source.

name: blit_nodes_and_flip_values
description: Waits for the blitter, sets two of its registers, then for each active node in a linked list with a non-negative word waits again and writes two node values into blitter registers, negating that word afterwards.

name: next_random_modulo_from_raster
description: Mixes the raster position from a hardware register into a global seed, rotates the seed left by one bit and returns it modulo the input value. Each call changes the seed for the next.

name: sum_table_entries_for_bytes
description: For ten bytes of a record, adds the 32-bit table entry indexed by each non-zero byte value and returns the total with its top bit cleared.

name: forward_to_single_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other work. It is a thin forwarding wrapper.

name: run_routine_per_mask_bit
description: Loops over four bits of a global mask and, for each set bit, calls an unnamed routine twice, waiting after each call for a flag word that another part of the program sets. It clears the flag word after each wait.

name: init_display_slots_from_constants
description: Calls one unnamed routine, stores fixed constants into several globals and pointer slots, calls another routine depending on a mode word, then copies sixteen longwords from a source table into the current record.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_to_buffer
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a table selected by an index in the current record into the buffer that record points to. It is the copy tail used by the sibling routine.

name: clear_216_bytes_from_record
description: Clears 216 consecutive bytes starting at a record base address. It is a simple block clear with no calls.

name: advance_match_and_load_stage
description: Searches up to a hundred steps for a value matching the record's table entries, and on a match advances a stage counter in the record, sets a timing constant by stage and copies stage values into globals before returning. It first forwards to an unnamed routine when a flag is set.

name: advance_match_and_load_stage
description: Performs the same table search, stage advance and global value copy as its sibling routine, without the leading flag check. It returns once a match is handled.

name: count_linked_list_nodes
description: Walks a circular linked list from a global head until it returns to the head, and returns the number of nodes plus one.

name: select_slot_copy_pending_entry
description: Takes a pending index from a global word and, when a flag is set, picks one of three destination slots by mode and the entry's position, then copies fields from the entry into that slot and sets a status byte of three or seven. It returns the pending index.

name: select_slot_and_copy_entry
description: When a flag word is set, picks one of three destination slots by mode and the entry's position value, then copies fields from the entry into that slot and sets a status byte to three or seven. It returns the value it was given when no slot is chosen.

name: step_entry_motion_with_bounds
description: Runs a per-frame motion step on a pending entry: it calls unnamed routines for each active flag, advances the position and velocity words within limits with bounce clamping, and returns early once the countdown expires. The motion results are stored back into the entry's record.

name: step_entry_motion_with_bounds
description: Performs the same bounded position and velocity step on an entry, bouncing values at limits and writing results to its record, with a countdown exit. It differs in how it reads its entry pointer.

name: reset_status_and_clear_counters
description: Clears a global status byte, clears two 16-bit counters and returns. The bit tests that follow read the byte just cleared, so the conditional table updates are never taken.

name: relink_entries_in_record_table
description: Walks a table of records spaced ninety-eight bytes apart, and for each entry not marked to skip it replaces links that match an old address with a new one, advancing a pointer by twice a stored value. It then sets a global flag bit.

name: format_number_and_copy_text
description: Stores a digit character derived from a data register, calls an unnamed formatting routine, then copies the resulting null-terminated text into the destination buffer. The text it formats is a printf-style long-decimal string.

name: call_indirect_with_word_argument
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored at a fixed offset from a global base, passing a word read from a fixed offset in the address-register block. It returns after the call.

name: call_indirect_routine
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored at a fixed offset from a global base and returns. It is a single indirect call.

name: format_long_text_then_restore
description: Sets a printf-style format string in a global buffer, calls an unnamed routine, then restores a different format string and increments a counter. It is a set-call-restore wrapper around that formatting call.

name: format_digit_and_copy_string
description: Writes a digit character derived from a data register into a table, calls an unnamed formatting routine, copies the resulting null-terminated text into the destination buffer and sets a counter to one.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Reads a per-object flag word and returns an early code for certain bits, otherwise checks a global key byte and returns a code accordingly. When a timer is running it calls an unnamed routine to read a status value and updates press and repeat counters.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Reads a per-object flag word and returns an early code for certain bits, otherwise checks a global key byte and returns a code accordingly. When a timer is running it calls an unnamed routine through the low-level library to read a status value and updates press and repeat counters.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Performs the same input classification as its sibling routines, returning early codes from flag bits and a key byte, and reading status through the low-level library when a timer runs. It updates the same press and repeat counters.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Performs the same input classification as its sibling routines, returning codes from flag bits and a key byte and updating press and repeat counters. Status is read through the low-level library call when a timer is running.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Performs the same input classification as its sibling routines, returning codes from flag bits and a key byte and updating press and repeat counters. Status is read through the low-level library call when a timer is running.

name: classify_input_status_code
description: Performs the same input classification as its sibling routines, reading status through the low-level library and touching the keyboard serial register. It returns codes from flag bits and a key byte and updates press and repeat counters.

name: delay_fixed_loop_count
description: Spins in a countdown loop of about three thousand iterations and returns, doing no other work. It is a fixed-length delay.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_to_buffer
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a table selected by an index in the object into the buffer the object points to, when the object's state word is zero. It is the same table copy as its sibling routines.

name: poll_keyboard_codes_in_loop
description: Loops on frame flags, reading keyboard codes from a global and comparing them against a long list of key values; certain keys reset counters and branch to a setup section that clears globals and reinitialises state. It touches the keyboard serial register, and the listing is cut off so the tail is not evident.

name: run_timed_sequence_until_key
description: Advances a timed sequence each frame by updating counters and velocity-like word pairs, waiting on a frame flag between steps. It stops when a particular key code is read or a position counter passes a threshold, then runs the same setup and cleanup as its sibling routine.

name: start_blit_from_pointer_slot
description: Waits for the blitter to go idle, loads the source pointer from a stored slot, writes a fixed value and mask words, sets a fixed size and starts the blit. It takes no arguments.

name: start_blit_at_offset_address
description: Waits for the blitter, computes a destination address from a stored pointer plus a fixed offset, writes it with fixed control, mask and size values into blitter registers, then waits until the blit finishes.

name: update_three_clamped_levels
description: Waits for the blitter and sets fixed registers, calls a function pointer for each item in a list, packs three four-bit values into a word, then adds velocity values to three accumulator pairs. Each accumulator is clamped at zero and each level is clamped at fifteen.

name: scale_points_by_divisor
description: For each entry in a list of coordinate pairs, shifts each value left by five bits, divides it by a divisor, adds an offset, and stores the results in two output arrays. It returns once the list is consumed.

name: rotate_and_project_point_list
description: Wraps an angle index within seven hundred twenty steps, looks up two table values, then for each point applies a rotation with shifts, divides by a perspective divisor and adds an offset. The screen coordinates go to two output arrays.

name: clip_segment_to_bounds
description: Clips a line segment against four bounds, computing intersection points with divisions and replacing endpoints that lie outside. It returns early when both ends fall outside the same bound; the listing is cut off before its end.

name: clip_segment_to_bounds
